stories.headline: Sarvam Defends Hosting Chinese AI Models, Releases Upgraded 105B Model
stories.script: Our lead story today. Sarvam AI co-founder Pratyush Kumar has responded to criticism of the company's decision to offer foreign-built open-weight models, Chinese ones among them, on its inference platform, Token Factory. Writing on X, he also explained how Sarvam had used computing capacity made available through the government's IndiaAI Mission, Analytics India Magazine reports. Sarvam introduced Token Factory earlier this month. It gives developers access to open-weight AI models running on infrastructure based in India. Its selection includes models from the Chinese firms DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Z.ai and Alibaba, as well as Google's Gemma and Sarvam's own models. Including foreign models led some to ask whether Sarvam was moving away from building homegrown foundation models and toward supplying AI infrastructure instead.
stories.whyThisMatters: Sarvam AI co-founder Pratyush Kumar has responded to criticism of the company's decision to offer foreign-built open-weight models, Chinese ones among them, on its inference platform, Token Factory.
keyPoints: Sarvam Defends Hosting Chinese AI Models, Releases Upgraded 105B Model

stories.headline: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
stories.script: In other news. Journalist Paris Marx examines data centers and generative AI in a new book called Hyperscale. In it, he takes readers inside the facilities and traces how computing infrastructure that has existed for decades has recently become politically explosive. The book arrives as local opposition to new data centers grows, according to TechCrunch. Speaking to TechCrunch, Marx called the expansion of data centers "fundamentally unsustainable" and said it was incompatible with a planet people can live on. He also argued that the sites are an easy target for wider frustration with the technology industry, because when one goes up in a community it is a physical, tangible presence. He said this holds true whatever a person's political views.
stories.whyThisMatters: Journalist Paris Marx examines data centers and generative AI in a new book called Hyperscale.
keyPoints: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
TechCrunch

stories.headline: Zhipu rolls out GLM-5.4 with vision and million-token context
stories.script: In China. Chinese AI company Zhipu has added a new model, GLM-5.4, to its Coding Plan subscription service, TechNode reports. The model showed up in the service's model menu on Monday, listed with vision support and a context window of one million tokens. Zhipu says it brings visual understanding and stronger performance on coding tasks. A member of the company's operations team said Zhipu had spent the past three months scaling up both the size of its models and its Loop Transformer approach. Subscribers on the V2, V3 and team plans have had their GLM-5.4 usage allowance raised by 50 percent. Zhipu has not yet published a full technical write-up covering the model's architecture, parameter count or benchmark results.
stories.whyThisMatters: Chinese AI company Zhipu has added a new model, GLM-5.4, to its Coding Plan subscription service, TechNode reports.
keyPoints: Zhipu rolls out GLM-5.4 with vision and million-token context
TechNode

stories.headline: L&T Technology Services Launches AI Toolchain for Software-Defined Vehicles
stories.script: Turning to India. L&T Technology Services, known as LTTS, has introduced an AI-driven engineering toolchain to help companies develop and validate software-defined vehicles, Analytics India Magazine reports. The platform, SDVault.ai, uses more than 250 AI agents across 12 engineering areas. These include requirements, system architecture, functional safety, cybersecurity, software development and testing. It belongs to the company's EI for Engineering suite and runs on its EIOne Engineering Intelligence platform. LTTS said safety-critical work is handled by a mix of AI agents and rule-based automation, and that engineers keep the final say on design decisions, verification and certification. The launch is part of a wider move by services firms to use AI in automotive software. In October, for example, HCLTech launched a validation service for software-defined vehicles powered by NVIDIA, which uses AI agents and virtual simulations to automate parts of the testing process.
stories.whyThisMatters: L&T Technology Services, known as LTTS, has introduced an AI-driven engineering toolchain to help companies develop and validate software-defined vehicles, Analytics India Magazine reports.
keyPoints: L&T Technology Services Launches AI Toolchain for Software-Defined Vehicles
Analytics India Magazine

stories.headline: San Francisco is enjoying an AI boom, but worries about a crash are growing
stories.script: Around the world. Artificial intelligence is driving a revival in San Francisco, the BBC reports, though concern is rising that the boom could end in a crash. The city lost many residents during the pandemic, and remote work left its downtown weakened. AI is now the main force behind its recovery, and other businesses are feeling the benefit. One of them belongs to Lauren Goldboss, who owns a small dog-walking company in the city. She has been taking on staff and buying vans, helped by Paw Perk, her new service that walks dogs for offices and has proved popular with several local AI start-ups. Two leading AI firms, OpenAI and Anthropic, have their headquarters in San Francisco. Both have been recruiting top engineers, often on very large salaries.
stories.whyThisMatters: Artificial intelligence is driving a revival in San Francisco, the BBC reports, though concern is rising that the boom could end in a crash.
keyPoints: San Francisco is enjoying an AI boom, but worries about a crash are growing
BBC

stories.headline: Ant Group unveils AI health ring and wristband under Afu brand
stories.script: In China. Afu, Ant Group's AI health service, has moved into wearable devices with the launch of a smart ring and a wristband, TechNode reports. The products were unveiled on Monday at the Afu healthcare ecosystem conference. Both monitor sleep, heart rate, breathing and blood oxygen, and use AI to turn those readings into health reports and recommendations. The wristband, known in Chinese as Fuhuan, will come in two versions, one with a screen and one without. The ring, called Fujie, has a plain silver-white look. Ant stressed that both devices have long battery life, but its announcement gave no detailed battery figures, prices or release dates. Afu said it was open to working with partners on the products.
stories.whyThisMatters: Afu, Ant Group's AI health service, has moved into wearable devices with the launch of a smart ring and a wristband, TechNode reports.
keyPoints: Ant Group unveils AI health ring and wristband under Afu brand
TechNode

stories.headline: Ant Group leads 100 million dollars round in humanoid startup Simplexity Robotics
stories.script: Next. Chinese robotics startup Simplexity Robotics has raised 100 million dollars in a pre-Series A round led by Ant Group, giving it a valuation of 1.6 billion dollars . Chairman and co-founder Wang Kai disclosed the deal to Bloomberg, TechNode reports. Existing backers including Tencent, HSG and Lanchi Ventures also took part. The company was founded by former Li Auto executives and is building robots and embodied AI.
stories.whyThisMatters: Chinese robotics startup Simplexity Robotics has raised $100 million in a pre-Series A round led by Ant Group, giving it a valuation of $1.6 billion.
keyPoints: Ant Group leads 100 million dollars round in humanoid startup Simplexity Robotic
TechNode

stories.headline: How Nvidia's billion-dollar turnaround in China is threatened by Huang's exit
stories.script: Elsewhere. After US export bans cost it billions of dollars in sales, Nvidia rebuilt its business in China's fast-growing AI sector by selling less powerful chips and software. That recovery is now at risk from the scandal around former chief executive Jensen Huang, The Economic Times reports. Universities, companies and research institutes in China have been buying more Nvidia products to run AI models for everything from business software to humanoid robots. Its most advanced AI processors, meanwhile, remain mostly out of reach for Chinese buyers. That is based on industry sources and a Reuters review of more than 100 Chinese corporate filings and procurement records. People familiar with the matter say some Chinese customers have cancelled or delayed orders since Huang's sudden resignation, putting billions in revenue at risk. US government scrutiny of Nvidia has also increased since he left.
stories.whyThisMatters: After US export bans cost it billions of dollars in sales, Nvidia rebuilt its business in China's fast-growing AI sector by selling less powerful chips and software.
keyPoints: How Nvidia's billion-dollar turnaround in China is threatened by Huang's exit

stories.headline: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
stories.script: From the research desk. The researchers behind a paper titled cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction look at how information should be blended inside AI models. It builds on an approach called manifold-constrained hyper-connections, which splits a model's shortcut pathways into several parallel streams. To keep training stable, the rules for mixing those streams are restricted to a particular mathematical set of matrices. The researchers found a trade-off. If the streams are mixed too little, they end up acting almost independently. If they are mixed too much, they become hard to tell apart.
stories.whyThisMatters: The researchers behind a paper titled cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction look at how information should be blended inside AI models.
keyPoints: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
